title: Identification under Observed Context-Specific Independence with Fixed Treatment and Outcome Assignments
banked_reason: The advertised complete state-specific identification procedure is not delivered: the theorem that would make the finite search exhaustive and complete is explicitly left open.
gap_reasons: The advertised complete state-specific identification procedure is not delivered: the theorem that would make the finite search exhaustive and complete is explicitly left open.
The binary-sink results prove only that an already accepted row-space certificate is sound; they do not show that every unidentified query in that slice produces such a certificate.
The two rational examples validate boundary behavior but do not establish a general forest-to-obstruction characterization.
proof_attempt_summary: The run replaced a circular countermodel certificate with a graph/CSI-derived affine nullspace construction and established a sound fixed-nuisance binary-sink slice, positive rational witnesses, and a careful observed-root comparator bridge. It did not prove that residual forests always yield a jointly positive shared-row kernel direction, nor the converse recovery theorem needed for total termination. Local SUCCESS-grammar and activation-cell defects remain repairable, but repairing them would not lift the achieved incremental result to the field floor.
tldr: Fixed treatment and outcome assignments activate observed CSI information that variable-level identification can discard, but a local forest alone need not survive shared rows across contexts. In the settled fixed-nuisance binary-sink base case, the proved forest-to-kernel lift yields the verifier's canonical forest-supported rational null vector, and a positive baseline plus an explicit radius yields two global quotient-shared models with the same observed law and different queries. A new root-control bridge compiles maximal-regular observed-root labels into identical context graphs and row quotients and reproduces every successful published formula on the published class intersected with this note's fixed finite, strictly primitive-positive CPT class. The multi-block global dichotomy remains open and must be settled before any complete procedure is claimed.
gap: Tikka et al. give sound CSI calculus and show that separate context graphs are incomplete. Mokhtarian et al. prove completeness for observed root controls, not observed endogenous activations. Chen and Darwiche give sound state-specific procedures without a complete obstruction theorem, and a local forest can be neutralized by cross-context row sharing.
fill: The project first certifies the exact binary-sink lifting step through a forest-restricted row-space alternative and baseline perturbation, then asks whether provenance-carrying Q-factor recovery and partial traces force an analogous global multi-block dichotomy.
